items.title: Explainer: Why buying power at Rs 37 per unit has sparked a political storm in Tamil Nadu
items.summary: The Tamil Nadu government’s decision to purchase power for up to Rs 37 per unit has triggered a big political row, prompting criticism over whether it was a result of poor planning or corruption. This is the highest cost of power paid in Tamil Nadu’s history, and is highly unusual for almost any state discom in the country. The Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK) government has cited an unexpected high demand amid a prolonged summer due to the El Niño phenomenon as the reason for the high cost. According to the Energy Resources Minister CTR Nirmal Kumar, the state’s peak power demand shot up by almost 30% from around 16,800 MW in October 2025 to nearly 21,700 MW this October – an additional requirement of nearly 5,000 MW. But the El Niño crisis has been felt across India, including the neighbouring south Indian states. Critics have compared the situation with that of Andhra Pradesh to question the lack of prior planning. Andhra Pradesh, too, is facing a surge in demand and had to resort to short-term power procurement deals. However, the state took measures as early as the first week of September.
